challenge.better_approach: Looked: the smaller alternative is to run the verdicts on Linux, which measures the wrong box (clause 2 is green on Windows). Another is a path shim at each reader; resolve_berth is already the one door and verdict_contract._open_ref uses it, so reusing it in _dispose is the smallest change.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That the commons copy of the berth (carry_berth) exists and is byte-identical when the verdict runs; the proof's fixture must include a missing-copy case that still refuses loudly. Also that _dispose is the only remaining direct open (verdict.py and the door are to be grepped by the build).
challenge.prior_art: In-house: verdict_contract._open_ref (4e84a96955a1) and sail.validate_path (1e99a571dd6d, d86b4e5ae614) already resolve far-box refs through chain.resolve_berth; the gate's _dispose is the second unfixed site of the same bug. Checked chain.resolve_berth source and gate.py:_dispose.
challenge.real_collision: None found: no intention says the verdict gate must read the recorded path; Law 7 is kept because an unresolvable ref still raises the recorded path's own error.

answers.falsifier: A verdict run on Windows for a ticket whose validate berth was recorded at a /home/akien/... path reads the commons copy and runs its instruments (8e0c, 35bb, 1eee verdicts berth); the fixture proof reds on Linux with _dispose unfixed and greens once fixed.
answers.from_idea: none, because it is a measured bug: akiendell 2026-11-19, `sail.py verdict 8e0cfb77827c` refused at the verdict gate, logged in CairnCommons/tickets/8e0cfb77827c-*.log.jsonl (82452b802); sibling fix 1e99a571dd6d
answers.how: In cairn/devices/codemother/machines/chart_gate/gate.py _dispose, open packet['validate_ref'] and validate['hypothesize_ref'] through chain.resolve_berth (the way verdict_contract._open_ref already does) instead of Path(ref).read_text; red-first proof as a fixture with a PureWindowsPath/Linux-style recorded ref and a commons copy, so it reds on Linux too.
answers.traces_to: Law 3 (nothing is known until measured: a Windows verdict is the measurement clause 2 of 8e0c/35bb/ca51/1eee asks for) and Law 7 (the refusal is loud and permanent); outline 9.4.8.1 on far-box berths; sibling tickets d86b4e5ae614, 4e84a96955a1, 1e99a571dd6d.
answers.what: The codemother verdict gate resolves a validate berth (and the hypothesize berth it names) recorded on another host through chain.resolve_berth, as sail.validate_path does, so a verdict run on a box other than the one that charted reads the commons copy instead of refusing.

bullets.text: gate.py _dispose reads validate_ref and hypothesize_ref with Path(...).read_text: the second site of the far-box berth bug after sail.verdict (1e99).
A refused Windows verdict moved 8e0c to FIXME:waiting and cast trouble ticket-refused-8e0cfb77827c-at-verdict; FIXME is the honest state, answered after this fix lands.
